field_decision: Ash over biogenic structures; panel includes the substrate. Exact station coordinates and thickness contacts require the cruise log or a calibrated original plate.
Ash in an excavated cone; the Hess 0.8–0.9 cm interval supplies station thickness.
Surface trace and stratified hyperpycnal cap on ash. Co-located with the early 17921 group.
Current-affected scratch-mark surface. No quantitative observation of 1991 fallout here.
Original thickness reconstructed by the author following complete mixing. Accepted as W08-404 at the Hess group 11 station. Photo extends 8 cm.
Deep trace-fossil window at the 17920 group. Existing interval.
Ash inside local holes and feeding burrows. Reworked thickness and sampled depth do not bound the unmixed local fallout.
Burrows within ash. Existing Hess group 5 and Wiesner station supply the principal range.
Ash below a remobilized cap; the deeper panel is sandy turbidite. Fig. 6C starts below the sediment surface; total ash contacts and retention unresolved.
Ash associated with burrowing and hyperpycnal cover. Sampled 0–5 cm window includes non-target sediment and has no stated full ash thickness.
Primary ash below a burrowed hyperpycnal cap. Cannot assign the composite 0–4.5 cm window to original ash.
Multiple turbidites cover the ash. Observed total section includes them. Duplicate of Wetzel 2009 fig. 6C.
Post-eruption turbidites and a marked ash base. Direct Hess thickness is questioned; sampled depth 8–16 cm crosses stratigraphic units.
Ripples identify reworked ash; organic surface cover after a bloom gives no original fallout thickness.
Fe/Mn enrichments and open tubes at redox boundary. No discrete original ash reading.
Surface flocs burrows and cones document preservation. Hess group 21 supplies an interval.
Vertical and horizontal sections show ash and ash-filled burrows; different levels include mass-flow sediment. Exact position and full original-bed contacts unresolved.
Deep trace fossils in muddy mass-flow sediment. These structures alone give no reading of original ash.
